_comment: The landing page in English, and the file the other three are checked against.
Values are HTML: they carry the links, <code> and emphasis that belong to the
sentence, because where a link falls inside a sentence is the sentence's
business and moves when it is translated. Everything structural — the
sections, the mock, the table — stays in site/index.html.
What is deliberately absent: the game names, platform names and the summary
in the picture. Those are RomM's own metadata, which the demo shows in
English whatever language the interface is in, and translating them here
would make the picture claim something the demo does not do.
page.title: RomMix — a Big Picture front end for RomM
page.description: Browse your RomM library like a console dashboard on a desktop, a handheld or a television. Download a game, play it, and your saves go back to RomM when you quit.
hero.title: Your RomM library, wherever you play.
hero.lede: A Big Picture–style front end for your own RomM server. Browse your library like a console dashboard, download a game, play it — and your saves go back to RomM when you quit.
hero.note: The demo is the real interface, browsing the homebrew library on RomM's public demo. Nothing to install, and no server needed. Use the arrow keys and Enter, a mouse, or a controller if one is plugged in.
devices.title: Desktop, handheld, television
devices.lede: One build for all three. RomMix opens fullscreen and everything in it can be reached with a D-pad, so the only real difference is how far away you are sitting.
devices.desk.title: At the desk
devices.desk.body: One download on any Linux desktop. Keyboard, mouse and controller all work, which is where most people set it up before it ever reaches a television.
devices.hands.title: In your hands
devices.hands.body: On a Steam Deck or any Linux handheld. Add the launcher script to Steam as a non-Steam game, and it opens in game mode with the built-in controls driving it.
devices.room.title: Across the room
devices.room.body: Runs under gamescope, and scales up on a 4K screen so everything still reads from the sofa. Sign in by scanning a code with your phone.
does.title: What it does
does.lede: RomM holds your library. RomMix puts it on a screen you can drive from the sofa, and gets the files where your emulator will find them.
does.library.title: Your library, laid out for a screen
does.library.body: Shelves for what you were last playing, what is already on this device and your favourites — then everything on the server, searchable and filtered by platform.
does.downloads.title: Downloads into your emulator's own folder
does.downloads.body: A game lands in its emulator's own ROM folder, SD card included, so it is there when you start that emulator yourself. Multi-disc sets are unpacked and the emulator is handed the playlist, not the first disc.
does.saves.title: Saves that follow you
does.saves.body: Newer saves come down before you play and go back up when you quit — after showing you what is about to be sent. Every game has a tab for pulling or pushing by hand.
does.emulators.title: The emulators, installed and assigned
does.emulators.body: Four of the five install from Settings, and RomMix picks which one runs each platform. Change that per platform whenever you like.
does.bios.title: BIOS from your own server
does.bios.body: Per platform: what is needed, what RomM has, and what is already in place — then RomMix installs the rest. Nothing comes from anywhere but your own server.
does.signin.title: Sign in from the couch
does.signin.body: RomMix shows a code and a QR. Approve it in RomM on your phone — no password typed on a television keyboard.
does.updates.title: It updates itself
does.updates.body: Nothing updates an AppImage for you. RomMix watches its own releases, says when one is out, and writes it over the file you run — ready at the next start. Or it just tells you, or nothing at all.
emulators.title: The emulators it drives
emulators.lede: Five, and RomMix works out which one runs each system. RetroDECK and EmuDeck each carry a dozen emulators; RetroArch runs one core per system; Eden and shadPS4 each run a single console. Settings → Platforms shows what every system will use, and lets you change it.
emulators.retrodeck: 79 systems, the NES to the PS3
emulators.emudeck: 74 systems, the NES to the Switch and 360
getting.title: Getting it
getting.lede: You need Linux, a RomM server at version 5 or newer, and one of the emulators above — RomMix can install all of them except EmuDeck. Download the AppImage for your machine from the releases page (x86_64 for a PC or a Steam Deck, arm64 for an ARM handheld) and run it. There is nothing to install.
getting.note: No version in the file name: updates are written over that same file, so shortcuts keep working. Settings says which version you have.
getting.steamBody: Download rommix-steam.sh from the same release, keep it beside the AppImage, and add the script as the non-Steam game — not the AppImage itself.
getting.steamNote: Steam cannot launch an AppImage directly; the script is what makes it work. The README covers building RomMix yourself, and what to do when an emulator will not start.
footer.disclaimer: RomMix is MIT-licensed, and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to RomM, any emulator it launches, or any console maker or game publisher. It ships no games: the covers on this page and the library in the demo come from RomM's own public demo, which is homebrew and freeware throughout, and each game's art and name belong to whoever made it. RomMix shows you what is on a server you run yourself.
